title: A smooth opaque screen fits the 2023 ASASSN-14ko X-ray ingress under tested flicker models
abstract: We test whether the resolved 2023 X-ray ingress of ASASSN-14ko separates intrinsic dimming from an opaque screen. We fit 57 published 2-ks EPIC-pn rate bins, including the bright and faint endpoints. A straight edge across a circular Gaussian source has a crossing scale of 0.60-0.62 observer days for flicker correlation times of 0-0.2 days. Its twice log likelihood advantage over a clipped exponential is 41.5 for independent flicker, 11.6 at 0.2 days, and near zero at 0.5-2 days. No calibrated significance is claimed. A circular uniform source also fits. A monotone decline admits a positive projected brightness profile behind an edge, so shape alone cannot identify dimming without source constraints. Under a steady Gaussian source and a rigid opaque strip at constant speed, 32 days below five percent requires a strip length of at least 56 source Gaussian widths for the 0.603-day fitted scale. This is a conditional value, not a confidence bound. The grey decline still excludes a uniform cold absorber but does not establish intrinsic shutdown. We provide source code, aggregate fits, figures and verified input retrieval. No new telescope data or orbital mechanism is claimed.
